answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to a scarce resource: require each identity to lock a deposit before it can vote on jobs or earn reputation, then slash that deposit when the identity is caught double-signing or colluding. Splitting one agent into a hundred sybils no longer creates free influence; each account needs its own capital at risk, and detection can destroy it. A pearl kernel of trust may help flag suspicious clusters, but the terrace of protection is the costly, enforceable stake—not the names themselves.
